data.title: Panthera expands Glasgow clinical research capacity
data.description:
Panthera has opened its expanded Glasgow Clinical Research Centre at the Health Innovation Hub, increasing capacity for commercial clinical research across Glasgow and the west of Scotland.

The UK’s largest independent clinical trial SMO marked the opening on 22 October with guests from healthcare, academia, government and industry. Dr Zubir Ahmed MP attended as Guest of Honour.

The purpose‑built centre includes eight clinical rooms, laboratory facilities and modern office space to support delivery of phase II and III trials for pharmaceutical sponsors and CROs. Panthera relocated from the Clinical Innovation Zone at Queen Elizabeth University Hospital earlier this year, with the new site expected to broaden opportunities for eligible patients to participate in studies of investigational treatments.

During the opening, Dr Ahmed spoke about the importance of clinical research infrastructure in maintaining Scotland’s leadership in medical research. Guests toured the facility and met Panthera staff to discuss trial delivery and ways to expand patient participation.

Dr Zubir Ahmed MP, Member of Parliament for Glasgow South West, said: “It was a pleasure to join Panthera to celebrate the opening of its expanded clinical research centre in Glasgow South West. I have first-hand experience of Glasgow’s proud history of medical innovation. Investment in facilities like this helps ensure our city remains at the forefront of developing new treatments and improving healthcare”

He added: “Clinical research has the potential to make a real difference to people’s lives, and it is particularly encouraging to see opportunities for patients in our local communities to participate in trials that could help shape the future of medicine.”

Stuart Young, CEO of Panthera, commented: “We are delighted to celebrate the official opening of our expanded Glasgow centre alongside colleagues and partners from across Scotland’s healthcare and life sciences community.”

He continued: “Glasgow has an outstanding reputation for medical research and innovation. This investment increases our capacity to deliver commercial clinical trials and reflects our confidence in the city’s research expertise.”

The centre sits within the Health Innovation Hub, developed by Kadans Science Partner with the Living Laboratory for Precision Medicine, supporting collaboration across Glasgow’s life sciences sector.

data.title: Exogenus leads €13 million EU project for secretome therapy
data.description:
The ExoCordOA consortium has launched a five‑year, €13 million Horizon Europe project to advance extracellular vesicle‑enriched secretome therapies towards clinical use, beginning with osteoarthritis.

Led by Exogenus Therapeutics, the initiative brings together ten organisations spanning biotechnology, clinical development, regulation, GMP manufacturing, imaging, academia and healthcare.

The consortium will combine these capabilities to support development of a new secretome‑based medicine for osteoarthritis and strengthen Europe’s position in regenerative and anti‑inflammatory therapeutics. A central objective is to progress Exogenus’ lead candidate, EXO‑101, towards clinical validation as a potential disease‑modifying treatment.

The programme will back the candidate’s phase 1 and 2 clinical development while addressing scientific, manufacturing, quality‑control and regulatory challenges that currently limit clinical translation of extracellular vesicle and secretome therapies.

It aims to resolve systemic bottlenecks by supporting more standardised approaches, robust analytical and potency assessment methods and a clearer regulatory pathway for future secretome‑based medicines.

Joana Correia, PhD, Co‑Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Exogenus Therapeutics, said: “ExoCordOA brings together the expertise needed not only to advance EXO-101 towards clinical validation in osteoarthritis, but also to tackle barriers affecting the wider secretome therapeutics field.”

She added: “As project coordinator, Exogenus is proud to lead this collaborative European effort to establish stronger scientific, manufacturing and regulatory foundations for a new generation of regenerative medicines.”

The consortium includes Lonza, Anthony Nolan, Eliquent Life Sciences, iLoF, Utrecht University, University Medical Center Utrecht, Maastricht University Medical Center+, Image Analysis Group and ReumaNederland.

data.title: Octane and Currus automate CAR T manufacturing on Cocoon
data.description:
Octane Biotech and Currus Biologics have completed the automation of the CUR‑001 manufacturing process on Octane’s Cocoon Platform. The transfer establishes a closed, reliable process designed to support consistent production as CUR‑001 enters clinical development.

The milestone follows FDA clearance of Currus’ IND application for CUR‑001, announced in September 2026. The approval enables a first‑in‑human, open‑label phase 1 basket trial in patients with mesothelin‑positive advanced refractory solid tumours. The first patient is expected to be dosed in early 2027.

CUR‑001 is the first clinical programme from Currus’ BEAT platform. It combines an autologous, FLAG‑tagged CAR T‑cell therapy targeting mesothelin with a BEAT bispecific antibody. The design is intended to activate CAR T‑cells in lymphoid tissue and counter the immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment that has limited CAR T‑cell therapy in solid tumours.

The companies have transferred the CUR‑001 process onto the Cocoon, Octane’s automated system for patient‑specific cell therapies. Moving to the Cocoon significantly reduced hands‑on operator time and the amount of viral vector required for each batch. This has produced a lower‑cost process that will support the programme as it advances.

Sam Cobb, Chief Executive Officer of Currus Biologics, said: “Getting IND clearance was a significant step forward. Ensuring we can make CUR‑001 reliably, patient after patient, is now our focus.”

He added: “The success of an autologous therapy depends heavily on the process behind it. Moving CUR‑001 onto the Cocoon gives us a consistent, closed process as we head into the clinic, and a manufacturing model that can grow with the programme.”

Louis Briggs, Vice President at Octane Biotech, explained: “Currus has a smart answer to one of the hardest problems in cell therapy, which is getting CAR T‑cells to work in solid tumours.”

He added: “Automating CUR‑001 on the Cocoon means fewer manual steps, less variability between batches and a process built to scale from phase 1 onward. We’re proud to support Currus as CUR‑001 moves toward its first patients.”

Octane and Currus will continue collaborating as CUR‑001 progresses through clinical development. The partnership aims to establish a reproducible manufacturing process and ultimately provide a new CAR T‑cell option for patients with hard‑to‑treat solid tumours.

For the phase 1 trial, CUR‑001 will be manufactured on the Cocoon at the Melbourne facility of Cell Therapies Pty Ltd. Technology transfer has already been completed, establishing readiness to support clinical manufacturing.

data.title: Regulatory filings for lung cancer therapy advance
data.description:
Hutchmed has confirmed that regulatory filings for Orpathys plus Tagrisso have been accepted for review in Europe and Japan.

The submissions aim to expand access to the targeted combination therapy for patients with locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer whose tumours show MET overexpression or amplification and who have progressed following EGFR‑TKI treatment.

In Europe, the EMA has validated and accepted the marketing authorisation application submitted by AstraZeneca. The filing seeks approval for patients whose disease has progressed on or after an EGFR‑TKI therapy.

In Japan, AstraZeneca has submitted a new drug application to the MHLW, which has also been accepted for review. The application covers patients with unresectable, advanced or recurrent disease who have MET overexpression or amplification and who have progressed following EGFR‑TKI therapy.

These steps follow the NDA submission to the FDA in September 2026 and mark further global regulatory momentum for the combination therapy.

The filings are supported by positive data from the global phase 3 Saffron trial. The results were presented at the ESMO Congress 2026 Presidential Symposium and published in The New England Journal of Medicine.

Orpathys plus Tagrisso delivered statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements in progression‑free survival and overall survival versus doublet platinum‑based chemotherapy in patients who had progressed on Tagrisso. The combination reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 45% compared to chemotherapy. Median progression‑free survival was 7.6 months versus 5.4 months for the comparator arm.

Results for overall survival showed a 32% reduction in the risk of death versus chemotherapy. Median overall survival was extended by 4.9 months, reaching 17.8 months versus 12.9 months. The safety profile was consistent with known data, with no new concerns reported.

Orpathys is jointly developed by AstraZeneca and Hutchmed and is commercialised by AstraZeneca.

data.title: Vertex wins MHRA backing for wider Casgevy use
data.description:
Vertex Pharmaceuticals has secured MHRA authorisation and reimbursement for expanded use of Casgevy for eligible children aged 5 to under 12 years with severe sickle cell disease or transfusion‑dependent beta thalassemia.

The decision makes exagamglogene autotemcel the first approved gene therapy available to eligible UK children as young as 5 years for both conditions.

A reimbursement agreement with NHS England, alongside updated guidance from NICE, means eligible patients can now access treatment in England. Vertex said the move strengthens its partnership with the UK health system, which first authorised Casgevy in 2023.

Nicola Massey, Executive Country Manager UK & Ireland, Vertex, said: “Since the UK became the first country to authorize CASGEVY in 2023, our partnership with the UK health system has helped bring this innovation to eligible people living with sickle cell disease and transfusion-dependent beta thalassemia.”

She added: “Today’s news reinforces our long-term commitment to these communities, enabling eligible younger children to access this innovative treatment earlier.”

Professor Josu de la Fuente, Professor of Practice at Imperial College London and Consultant Haematologist at Imperial College Healthcare NHS Trust, explained: “For children living with sickle cell disease or transfusion-dependent beta thalassemia, complications generally begin at a very young age and have lasting consequences.”

He continued: “Today’s approval is an important advance and offers new hope to eligible children and their families. It enables us to consider younger children for treatment earlier, before disease-related complications lead to lasting organ damage.”

Vertex is working with health authorities in Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland to extend access for eligible patients as quickly as possible.

data.title: Qureight calls for fibrosis burden to lead imaging biomarkers
data.description:
Qureight has published a peer‑reviewed viewpoint arguing that fibrosis extent should become the principal structural imaging biomarker in antifibrotic clinical trials.

The Cambridge‑based imaging company said the paper sets out a scientific and regulatory case for positioning fibrosis burden as the leading candidate for FDA biomarker qualification.

In fibrotic interstitial lung disease, pulmonary fibrosis causes scar tissue to accumulate, distorting the lung and reducing functioning tissue. Forced vital capacity is currently the primary registrational endpoint in antifibrotic trials. It has supported the approval and adoption of several therapies. However, FVC is a downstream measure of lung function influenced by factors beyond fibrosis.

In the Viewpoint, titled ‘Fibrosis extent on HRCT: the principal structural imaging biomarker for antifibrotic trials’, Qureight CSO Dr Simon Walsh explained: “If an antifibrotic is designed to slow the accumulation of scar tissue, trials should measure that scar tissue directly. Quantitative HRCT can show structural disease change that lung-function testing alone cannot.”

He added: “The opportunity now is to build the regulator-facing evidence needed to use fibrosis burden consistently and confidently across trials.”

The paper outlines how measuring fibrosis extent using imaging biomarkers for quantitative high‑resolution computed tomography can complement FVC by providing a more biologically proximate view of whether a therapy is slowing pulmonary fibrosis.

Qureight said that for fibrosis extent to become a surrogate endpoint, a more robust evidence base is required. This includes trial‑level data demonstrating a clear association between treatment‑driven changes in fibrosis accumulation and proof that slowing fibrosis progression predicts how patients feel, function or survive.

data.title: Hansa reports positive PAES results for Idefirix at ASN Kidney Week
data.description:
Hansa Biopharma has announced positive data from the European Post‑Authorization Efficacy and Safety study of Idefirix, presented in the High‑Impact Clinical Trials session at ASN Kidney Week 2026. The open‑label trial evaluated 50 crossmatch‑positive deceased‑donor kidney transplants across Europe and was selected as a late‑breaking abstract at the congress.

Renée Aguiar‑Lucander, CEO of Hansa Biopharma, said: “The presentation of the PAES study in the High-Impact Clinical Trials session highlights the scientific and clinical relevance of these findings and the potential of imlifidase to address a significant unmet need for highly sensitized patients awaiting kidney transplantation. We are encouraged by the continued interest from the transplant community in the growing body of evidence supporting imlifidase.”

The study reported a one‑year graft failure‑free survival rate of 90% at 12 months post‑transplant. Graft survival reached 92% and patient survival 98%, with Idefirix generally well tolerated and showing a safety profile consistent with previous clinical experience.

Oriol Bestard MD PhD, Vall d’Hebron University Hospital, Barcelona, and investigator for the trial, said: “The successful completion of the PAES study provides important evidence in a patient population that continues to face significant challenges in accessing kidney transplantation.

“These findings add to the clinical evidence supporting the use of imlifidase to enable transplantation in highly sensitized patients with a positive crossmatch against a deceased donor.”

ASN Kidney Week is one of the leading global scientific meetings in nephrology and transplantation, with the High‑Impact Clinical Trials session reserved for studies considered among the most clinically relevant at the congress. The abstract was presented by Dr Bestard on behalf of the PAES investigators.

data.title: Santersus advances nucleoCapture into pivotal sepsis study
data.description:
Santersus is advancing NUC‑CAP, a multicentre, randomised pivotal study of NucleoCapture, its investigational extracorporeal blood‑purification technology, in critically ill patients with sepsis and respiratory failure.

The trial is expected to enrol up to 350 patients across clinical sites in the United States and Europe, with Axcellant appointed as global CRO to support international execution.

Participants will be randomized 1:1 to receive either standard of care alone or standard of care plus NucleoCapture. The study will assess device‑related safety and a primary effectiveness endpoint combining all‑cause mortality through day 28 with organ support‑free days through day 28, analysed using win‑ratio methodology.

The aim is to determine whether selectively removing circulating neutrophil extracellular traps can improve outcomes for patients requiring intensive care.

NucleoCapture is designed to remove NETs from the bloodstream through selective extracorporeal adsorption. NETs contribute to innate immune defence but have also been associated with inflammatory and thrombotic processes and organ injury when excessive or dysregulated.

The clinical significance of targeting NETs remains to be established. According to World Health Organization estimates for 2017, ~48.9 million people developed sepsis worldwide and 11 million deaths were associated with the condition.

The pivotal programme follows earlier development, including completion of a first‑in‑human exploratory study. In 2022, NucleoCapture received FDA Breakthrough Device Designation as an adjunctive treatment to antibiotics in sepsis.

James Ladtkow, Chief Executive Officer of Santersus, said: “The advancement of NUC-CAP into pivotal development is a significant milestone for Santersus because it moves NucleoCapture into a rigorous, multinational clinical program designed to evaluate endpoints that matter in the treatment of critically ill patients.”

He added: “Our objective is to build a robust body of clinical evidence around a differentiated therapeutic approach: directly removing circulating NETs that are associated with inflammatory, thrombotic and organ-damaging processes.”

Wojciech Kula, CEO of Axcellant, said: “We are pleased to support Santersus in the global execution of NUC-CAP.”

He continued: “The study represents an important clinical undertaking in a critically ill patient population, and our team will bring integrated clinical-development capabilities to support disciplined execution across participating regions.”

Santersus is targeting an interim analysis in Q4 2027, followed by potential CE certification and an EU launch in Q2 2028. PMA submission is planned for Q2 2029, with potential FDA approval and a US launch in Q4 2029.

data.title: Hutchmed reports phase 3 SANOVO data for first‑line lung cancer
data.description:
Hutchmed has announced positive phase 3 results from the SANOVO trial evaluating ORPATHYS plus TAGRISSO in treatment‑naïve patients with EGFR‑mutated non‑small cell lung cancer and MET overexpression. The data, presented at ESMO Congress 2026, showed statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements in progression‑free survival compared with TAGRISSO alone.

Professor Yi‑Long Wu said: “The SANOVO results mark a pivotal evolution in how we approach first-line EGFR-mutated lung cancer. Historically, co-occurring MET alterations have been associated with poor outcomes on EGFR-TKI treatment, increasing the motivation to test for MET alterations at diagnosis and upon progression.

These potentially practice-changing results showed that adding savolitinib to osimertinib extended median PFS by more than a year in the high MET population, and 11 months overall, in first-line MET-overexpressing EGFR-mutated lung cancer.

“Coupled with highly encouraging clinical benefit in OS, these data reinforce the transformative potential of this all-oral, biomarker-directed treatment approach for a patient population where co-occurring MET overexpression may limit the long-term benefits of EGFR-TKI monotherapy.”

In the intention‑to‑treat population, the combination reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 44%, with median PFS reaching 24.9 months versus 13.8 months for TAGRISSO alone. In the high MET subgroup, risk reduction reached 55%, with median PFS of 24.8 months compared with 11.1 months. Overall survival also improved, with median OS of 44.5 months versus 34.9 months and three‑year survival rates of 67.4% versus 47.4%.

Mr Johnny Cheng, Acting Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer of Hutchmed, said: “SANOVO, alongside the SAFFRON and SACHI studies, establishes a comprehensive treatment continuum for the ORPATHYS plus TAGRISSO combination – spanning frontline intervention to post-EGFR-TKI resistance.

“SANOVO demonstrates that by identifying MET overexpression at diagnosis and initiating an all oral, dual-targeted combination upfront, we can meaningfully extend PFS and OS while preserving patient quality of life.”

data.title: Octane and Currus automate CUR‑001 manufacturing on cocoon platform
data.description:
Octane Biotech and Currus Biologics have automated the manufacturing process for CUR‑001 on Octane’s Cocoon platform, establishing a closed, reliable process to support consistent production as the therapy enters clinical development.

The milestone follows FDA clearance of Currus’ IND application, enabling a first‑in‑human, open‑label phase 1 basket trial in mesothelin‑positive advanced refractory solid tumours, with first patient dosing expected in early 2027.

CUR‑001 is the first clinical programme from Currus’ BEAT platform, combining an autologous, FLAG‑tagged CAR T‑cell therapy targeting mesothelin with a BEAT bispecific antibody. The design engages CAR T‑cells and antigen‑presenting cells to activate T‑cells in lymphoid tissue and counter the immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment that has limited CAR T‑cell therapy in solid tumours.

The companies have transferred the manufacturing process onto the Cocoon, Octane’s automated system for patient‑specific cell therapies. Moving to the platform significantly reduced hands‑on operator time and viral vector requirements, two major cost drivers in autologous CAR T‑cell manufacturing.

Sam Cobb, Chief Executive Officer of Currus Biologics, said: “Getting IND clearance was a significant step forward. Ensuring we can make CUR-001 reliably, patient after patient, is now our focus.”

He added: “The success of an autologous therapy depends heavily on the process behind it. Moving CUR-001 onto the Cocoon gives us a consistent, closed process as we head into the clinic, and a manufacturing model that can grow with the programme.”

Louis Briggs, Vice President, Octane Biotech, explained: “Currus has a smart answer to one of the hardest problems in cell therapy, which is getting CAR T-cells to work in solid tumours.”

He continued: “Automating CUR-001 on the Cocoon means fewer manual steps, less variability between batches and a process built to scale from phase 1 onward. We’re proud to support Currus as CUR-001 moves toward its first patients.”

CUR‑001 will be manufactured for the phase 1 trial at Cell Therapies Pty Ltd in Melbourne, where technology transfer has been completed and operational readiness established.
